answer: Each identity claims one cedar signal post on a mesa rim, locks a 75-credit bond to its serial, and files one signal pulse per epoch. A mesa relay records its strength; an auditor recomputes attenuation from a public cedar-canopy table using distance and depth, burning the bond for a mismatch over 5%, a reused serial, or a shared post. The first filing costs 39, the kth 39+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7032 and 1000 fakes pay 3,535,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-signal ring fails: a replayed pulse has the wrong attenuation for that post. An honest agent pays 39 once, bond refunded.
